headline: Bhutan Becomes First in Southeast Asia to Eliminate Dog-Transmitted Rabies
meta_description: Bhutan has achieved zero human deaths from dog-transmitted rabies since 2023, with WHO official validation marking a historic public health milestone.
summary_short: Bhutan has eliminated dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem, recording zero human deaths since 2023. WHO has now officially validated this achievement.
body:
Bhutan has eliminated dog-transmitted rabies as a public health problem, with zero human deaths recorded since 2023. The World Health Organization has now officially validated this achievement, making Bhutan the first country in Southeast Asia to reach this milestone.

The validation from WHO represents a significant recognition of sustained effort against a disease that has long threatened public health across the region. Bhutan's success demonstrates that systematic, coordinated approaches to rabies prevention—typically involving vaccination programs and public health infrastructure—can achieve complete elimination of transmission from dogs to humans.

This accomplishment stands out as a rare public health victory in a region where rabies remains endemic in many neighboring countries. The official WHO validation underscores Bhutan's commitment to protecting its population and sets a benchmark for other nations working toward similar goals.
